title: CapabilityStatusV1
description: FND-002 task 3: the explicit unavailable-capability record served by GET /capabilities (document 13 section 12.3, shared foundation FND-010 task 6). Its whole reason to exist is that an absent capability must be VISIBLE: document 08 section 9 requires a typed capability_unavailable and states it 'must never trigger a silent fallback to a different method', and document 09 section 2.1 forbids returning 'a different method or an empty success result'.

unavailable_reason.$comment: IMP-DEC-FND002-010: the UNION of five overlapping prose lists the specification never reconciles. KAG gateway section 4 gives seven ('not installed, disabled, unentitled, unhealthy, optional provider absent, unqualified and temporarily unavailable'); document 12 section 5 adds 'degraded'; terminology broker section 14 adds 'stale projection' and 'rights-unavailable'. The union is taken rather than any one list because the failure direction matters: a reason set that is too WIDE can only ever make a state more precisely reported, while a set that is too narrow forces a real state to be reported as a neighbouring one — which is the 'unavailable presented as success' class this record exists to prevent.

available_requires_the_full_chain.$comment: A capability cannot report itself currently available while any prerequisite in the installed -> enabled -> qualified chain is false. Without this, 'available: true, qualified: false' is a well-formed record, and that is exactly the shape a silent substitution takes: an unqualified method answering in place of a qualified one. Document 20 section 8 ('Emergency disable stops new execution ... it does not silently switch methods') and scientific processor section 9 ('disabling provider yields stable capability_unavailable and never substitutes a different method') are the rules this makes structural.

unavailable_requires_a_reason.$comment: Required iff unavailable, forbidden iff available. Shared foundation FND-010 task 6 requires /capabilities to expose 'reason-code states'; document 13 section 12.3 requires 'reason codes'; document 15 section 9 requires the catalogue to report 'its disabled/unavailable reason'. An unavailable capability with no reason is the empty measurement again: it reports the absence without reporting anything actionable, and a consumer cannot distinguish 'not entitled' from 'provider down'.

method_id.$comment: The specific method inside the capability, when the record is method-scoped.

installed.$comment: Present in the deployed image's signed contribution catalogue (document 13 section 12.1).

qualified.$comment: Has a current qualification report. An unqualified method is unavailable, never silently downgraded.

available.$comment: Currently answerable. This is the member a caller acts on, and it is deliberately separate from readiness: document 09 section 3.4 and document 13 section 12.4 both state that optional-provider failure appears HERE and 'does not make the base service unready'. A consumer that maps this onto a health probe reintroduces the accidental 404/502 that KAG gateway section 4 forbids.

required_for_publication.$comment: IMP-DEC-FND002-011: the specification requires the BEHAVIOUR in four places (document 09 section 8, document 12 section 9, research output section 10, document 14 section 6.4: 'a required unavailable capability blocks approval-ready state') and never names a member for it. Without a member the blocking rule has nothing to read, so it is released here and required: 'optional by default' would make every capability silently non-blocking, which is the failure direction the rule exists to prevent.

provider_health.$comment: Optional-provider health, reported without leaking upstream topology (KAG gateway section 3: 'typed timeout/unavailable distinctions without leaking upstream topology'). No host, endpoint or error text.

qualification_report_ref.$comment: The exact qualification report. A PinnedVersionRef, never a floating IdentityRef: document 16 section 3.3 requires an exact immutable reference wherever reproducibility depends on it.
